label: int_literal_limit
graph_version: 3.9.8 (3.9.7 + one primary per misconception (S9c) and the four remaining sibling edges (S9b), 2026-11-04; listed in revision_3_9_8)

edges.label:
[0] everyday_reading (E): Folk meaning: in maths any string of digits names a number, and a very large number simply 'becomes' a bigger kind of number. Java rule: a digit sequence without an L suffix is an int literal and must denote a value in -2147483648..2147483647; 2147483648 is legal only as the operand of unary minus (-2147483648), and 3000000000 does not compile (write 3000000000L).
[1] misconception (M) -> LargeIntegerLong: wrong rule: A large integer literal is automatically long. Right rule: A digit sequence is an int literal only if its value lies within the int range; a larger literal such as 3000000000 is a compile-time error unless written with the L suffix (3000000000L), and the book advises the long type for values of ten digits or more.
[2] inconsistent_trace (T) -> LargeIntegerLong: Points to LT (the compiler checks each literal's value against the int range when it reads the token, before any code runs). Applied unevenly: the student accepts one out-of-range literal as 'automatically long' but rejects another, or treats -2147483648 as illegal because 2147483648 alone is illegal, or expects the range check to apply to computed values such as 2147483647 + 1 (which compiles and wraps). (here mixing in: "a large integer literal is automatically long")

[0] names_the_element (N): An int literal is a lexical constant: a source-code representation of an int value, written as decimal digits (optionally signed) whose value lies within the int range.
[1] states_the_rule (S): A digit sequence is an int literal only when its decimal value lies between -2147483648 and 2147483647 inclusive; the magnitude 2147483648 may appear only as -2147483648; larger literals need the long suffix L.

[0] line_by_line_trace (LT): At compile time the compiler reads the digit token, converts it to a value and checks the range; at run time the literal is simply evaluated to that fixed value, and a leading minus is applied as unary negation to the literal's value.
[1] output_prediction (OP): A legal int literal evaluates to the int value it denotes (2147483647 is int 2147483647; -2147483648 is int Integer.MIN_VALUE); an out-of-range literal has no value because the program does not compile.
[2] one_step_execution (OS): Evaluating a literal changes no variable and always yields the same int; in int x = 2147483647; the only state change is x receiving that value.

[0] relation_to_neighbour (R): The general literal rule (a source-code representation of a value) is constrained here by int's range: a digit sequence outside -2147483648..2147483647 is not a valid int literal and must be written as a long literal with L.
[1] relation_to_neighbour (R): The literal limit is exactly int's 32-bit range, but it is checked only for literals: the literal 2147483648 is a compile-time error, whereas the expression 2147483647 + 1 compiles and overflows at run time to -2147483648.
[2] purpose_of_the_whole (P): Used to write a fixed integer constant directly in code (Sajaniemi role: fixed value), including the extreme values; for the limits themselves the named constants Integer.MAX_VALUE and Integer.MIN_VALUE are clearer.

[0] predict_a_change (C) -> LargeIntegerLong: Adding one digit or one unit can push a literal out of range (2147483647 compiles, 2147483648 does not), and adding a leading minus can bring it back (-2147483648 compiles); rewriting the literal as the expression 2147483647 + 1 compiles but silently wraps. Invariant: the range check is applied to literal tokens at compile time, never to computed values.
[1] transfer_to_a_new_program (X): Use a plain int literal for whole-number constants comfortably inside about plus or minus 2.1 billion; when values may reach ten digits use long with L-suffixed literals; for the extreme values use Integer.MAX_VALUE and Integer.MIN_VALUE rather than typing the digits.
[2] diagnose_an_error (D): rule broken: An int literal must lie within the int range. Kind: compile-time. Trigger class: A digit sequence (without L) whose value exceeds 2147483647, or 2147483648 written without a leading minus, e.g. int big = 3000000000; (javac: integer number too large).

wrong: A whole-number literal that is too big for an int automatically becomes a long. | right: A sequence of digits is an int literal only if its value falls within the int range; for larger values the book advises the long type.

The limit on int literals is int's 32-bit range, -2147483648 to 2147483647.
An int literal is legal only if its value lies within the int range, so a digit sequence outside -2147483648..2147483647 is not a valid int literal.
